item.title: Gunmen kill 51-year-old man, two others in fresh Plateau attack
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Gunmen have killed three persons in a fresh attack on Nkiedowro community in Teegbe District of Bassa Local Government Area of Plateau State, throwing residents into mourning. The attack, which occurred on Friday night, claimed the lives of three Irigwe natives, bringing to 20 the number of Irigwe people reportedly killed within the week, according to the National Publicity Secretary of the Irigwe Youth Movement, Joseph Chudu Yonkpa. Yonkpa, who confirmed the killings in a statement made available to newsmen on Saturday, said the attackers launched two separate ambushes on the community. “Yesterday night, Fulani militias launched two separate ambushes at Nkiedowro, Teegbe District, killing three Irigwe natives,” he said. He identified the victims as Ngudo Kura, 51; Hosea Ishaya, 26; and Naomi Izeh, 22. “This makes it a total of 20 Irigwe people killed this week in an unprovoked manner,” Yonkpa added. He expressed condolences to the families of the victims and the entire Irigwe community, praying for the repose of the souls of the deceased. Our correspondent reports that the latest killings occurred barely two days after 17 persons were given a mass burial following an attack on the Tafi Gana community, also in Bassa Local Government Area. The development has heightened concerns over the security situation in the area, with residents reportedly apprehensive about possible further attacks. The Irigwe Youth Movement urged residents to remain vigilant and avoid movements that could expose them to danger. “We call on our people to intensify vigilance, avoid late-night and isolated movements, and report suspicious movements to the relevant authorities,” Yonkpa said. The group also appealed to security agencies to strengthen surveillance and take necessary measures to protect communities in the area. Efforts to get the reaction of security operatives were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. item.title: INEC Declares Readiness For 2027, Expresses Satisfaction With Plateau Mock Election
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has declared its readiness for the 2027 general elections, assuring Nigerians that it is committed to conducting free, inclusive, credible and transparent polls. INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, gave the assurance while monitoring Saturday’s mock election in Plateau State, where he expressed satisfaction with the turnout of voters and the conduct of the exercise. Amupitan said the mock election was designed to test the functionality of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV), as well as assess the efficiency of the accreditation process ahead of the 2027 general elections. INEC Chairman Amupitan inspecting the exercise in Jos on Saturday, November 28, 2026. He commended voters for their orderly conduct, expressing delight at seeing an elderly woman turn out for the exercise and successfully undergo accreditation. “You can see yourself that the turnout is very good. What we are trying to test is actually the working of the machines, which are the BVAS and the IReV, and voters are being accredited. You can see how orderly it is going. From what we have seen, I am impressed,” he said. The INEC chairman acknowledged the support of the Plateau State Independent Electoral Commission in mobilising residents for the exercise but noted that the environmental sanitation exercise earlier scheduled for Saturday may have affected early participation, as some residents had indicated they would be unable to come out in time. On the commission’s preparedness for the 2027 elections, Amupitan said INEC was determined to deliver one of the best elections in the country’s history. “For the 2027 general elections, INEC is prepared, and I want to assure all Nigerians that we are going to have one of the best elections. We are determined that the 2027 election will be free, inclusive, credible and transparent,” he stated. Addressing concerns over the security situation in the country, the INEC chairman said the commission was working with relevant security agencies to ensure the protection of voters and electoral personnel during the forthcoming elections. He disclosed that INEC recently convened a one-day national security conference where stakeholders deliberated on security challenges and measures to safeguard the electoral process. INEC Chairman, Joash Amupitan, seen addressing staff and voters in Jos on Saturday, NOVEMBER 28, 2026. Amupitan further revealed that the commission had conducted a risk assessment of polling units across the country, with identified locations shared with law enforcement agencies to enable them to strengthen security arrangements ahead of the elections. “We have done what we call a risk assessment of all the polling units in Nigeria, and we have identified all the polling units and shared them with the law enforcement agencies so that they can make extra preparations ahead of the elections,” he said. item.title: Numbers ‘Impressive’ As Voters Turnout For INEC Mock Exercise In Kano
item.description: The mock accreditation for the 2027 general elections is underway in Paniso ward, Kano, as voters were seen turning out in seemingly impressive numbers for the exercise, compared to other regions in the country. Our correspondent, who monitored one of the selected polling units, noted that two INEC staff and two ad hoc personnel are testing the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices. Although voter turnout is still relatively low as against what is expected, the exercise is progressing smoothly, with no discrepancies reported and the BVAS thumbprint verification functioning as expected so far. Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Joash Amupitan, is currently in Jos to inspect the ongoing mock accreditation exercise, ahead of the 2027 general elections. It’s about seven weeks before the 2027 general election, and INEC is today running a nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise in all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). Professor Joash Amupitan, INEC Chairman, disclosed this at the INEC and Office of the National Security Adviser ONSA) Strategic Election Security Conference in Abuja on Thursday. According to him, the exercise would put the Commission’s new equipment and result systems under live conditions. “While this exercise allows INEC to stress-test our upgraded BVAS devices and verify our stricter INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) validation safeguards—which automatically block arithmetic inconsistencies and over-voting, it also serves as an essential live dry run for our security architecture,” he said. The presidential and National Assembly elections hold on 16 January 2027 across 177,299 polling units, with governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections to follow on 6 February 2027. item.title: Kano varsity bans students, lecturers from exchanging gifts
item.description: Northwest University, Kano, has prohibited students and lecturers from giving or receiving gifts in connection with university services, warning that anyone who violates the directive will face disciplinary action. The university classified the practice as corruption and serious misconduct, stressing that the ban applies to both staff and students, irrespective of the intentions behind the gifts. The Registrar, Isyaku Adamu, announced the directive in a statement issued on Friday, following public attention generated by reports of students presenting gifts to lecturers recognised as the best level coordinators or lecturers in their respective categories. According to the registrar, the practice could damage the institution’s reputation and violate provisions of its Service Conditions and Regulations (2025), as amended. The university specifically identified the giving and receiving of gifts as acts of corruption and conduct capable of bringing the institution into disrepute. “Consequently, any staff or students found involved in giving and/or receiving gift items for university services rendered will be charged with committing an act(s) of serious misconduct and the university will immediately initiate disciplinary process against the staff or students according to the university’s regulations,” Adamu said. He added that offenders would be liable to sanctions under Section 16 of the regulations. The registrar consequently urged members of the university community to observe the institution’s rules, ethical standards and best practices to avoid disciplinary action. He also called on staff and students to take the directive seriously, adding, “A stitch in time saves nine!” Northwest University, Kano, is a state-owned institution established by the Kano State Government in 2012. It was renamed Yusuf Maitama Sule University in 2017 before reverting to its original name in 2024 following an amendment to the state law establishing it. item.title: UEFA begins probe into Marseille, Besiktas fans clash
item.description: UEFA has opened disciplinary investigations into violent incidents involving supporters of Marseille and Besiktas during their respective Europa League fixtures on Thursday. The European football governing body announced the probes on Friday, following clashes between Marseille and Levski Sofia supporters in France and a confrontation between Besiktas fans and police in Georgia. In Marseille, several hundred home supporters confronted visiting Levski Sofia fans, leaving five Bulgarian supporters hospitalised. French magistrates have also launched an investigation into alleged intentional violence involving some Marseille supporters. Authorities are equally examining allegations of incitement to hatred following claims of Nazi salutes and provocations by Bulgarian fans. Meanwhile, Besiktas’ encounter with Israeli side Hapoel Beer-Sheva in Batumi, Georgia, was temporarily halted after clashes broke out between supporters and police. The incident followed the display of a pro-Palestinian banner bearing the inscription, “Revolt against the occupation, freedom for Palestine”, alongside Palestinian flags and chants against Israel. UEFA said the incidents contradicted its commitment to ensuring that football matches are played in an atmosphere of peace, mutual respect and sporting fairness. “The events witnessed at the above-mentioned matches run counter… to UEFA’s objective, enshrined in its Statutes, of ensuring that football matches are played in a spirit of peace, mutual respect and sporting fairness,” the governing body said. It added that it had appointed Ethics and Disciplinary Inspectors to investigate the incidents. The Besiktas fixture was moved from Istanbul to Georgia after Turkish authorities informed UEFA that the match could not be hosted in Turkey for safety and security reasons. The relocation came amid worsening diplomatic relations between Turkey and Israel following the outbreak of the Gaza war. item.title: 2027: SDP candidate promises N200 petrol, free healthcare
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), Dr Adewole Adebayo, has promised to reduce petrol prices to N200 per litre without subsidy and provide free healthcare if elected president in 2027. He also pledged free and compulsory education, increased food production, job creation and improved welfare for persons living with disabilities. Adebayo made the promises at an SDP town hall meeting with party leaders, candidates and supporters in Nasarawa State. He urged Nigerians to use the 2027 general election to determine the country’s leadership through the ballot, stressing the importance of electoral participation. Adebayo said the SDP had developed policy proposals to address poverty, unemployment, high living costs and other economic challenges facing the country. On fuel pricing, he said an SDP-led government would reduce petrol prices to N200 per litre without subsidy through improved efficiency and measures to address corruption in the petroleum sector. “We will give you petrol for N200 per litre without subsidy. We will sell it for N200, and NNPC will still make a profit because we will stop funding corruption,” he said. On agriculture, Adebayo said Nasarawa and neighbouring states had the potential to contribute significantly to national food production. “Nasarawa alone can feed Nigeria. Nasarawa, Plateau, Kogi, Kaduna and the Federal Capital Territory have the capacity to feed the whole of Africa,” he said. He also promised free and compulsory education, including measures to expand access to schooling for out-of-school children. According to him, an SDP administration would integrate children in the Almajiri system into formal education while ensuring they continued to receive religious instruction. On healthcare, Adebayo proposed establishing a Federal Medical Centre in every federal constituency and introducing compulsory medical check-ups four times annually. He also promised free medical consultations and medication, although he did not provide details of the proposed funding arrangements. On employment, the SDP candidate pledged to create more job opportunities, including for individuals living with disabilities. He also promised to develop Nasarawa’s mineral resources, including gold, coal, lithium and copper, to promote economic growth and improve the welfare of host communities. Adebayo endorsed the SDP governorship candidate in the state, former Inspector-General of Police, Abubakar Adamu, saying his experience in policing would be an asset in addressing security challenges. He urged voters to assess political candidates based on their records, character and policy proposals rather than party affiliations. The presidential candidate also called for an enabling environment for opposition parties to participate in the electoral process, stressing the importance of political competition in a democracy. item.title: Pete Edochie: Linc breaks down in tears as unusual calm rules Enugu residence
item.description: By Benjamin Njoku & By Dennis Agbo Linc Edochie, the third son of the late Pete Edochie, could not hold back his tears when he saw his father’s corpse in the mortuary. The movie legend died in the early hours of Wednesday after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. He had taken ill and was rushed to a hospital in Enugu, where he passed away. Painting a gloomy picture of the atmosphere at the late actor’s riverside residence in Trans-Ekulu, Enugu-based actor and filmmaker, Steve Eboh, said Linc broke down the moment he sighted his father’s body. “When Linc stormed the mortuary and sighted his father’s corpse, he cried profusely and leaned on his brother’s shoulder. We consoled him and prayed for the family,” Eboh said. Eboh added that grief was written all over the faces of people whose lives Pete Edochie had touched during his acting career. “We thank God for a life well spent. He was a legend who touched so many lives. He was not just an actor, he was a global icon. Everybody knew him.” Our correspondent, who visited the late actor’s Trans-Ekulu residence, described a gloomy picture of desertion and sorrow. “Apart from a domestic aide seen at the premises, there was little indication of the tragic development that had thrown the family and the Nigerian entertainment industry into mourning,” he noted. A source familiar with the circumstances surrounding his death told our correspondent that the actor took ill on Tuesday night and was subsequently rushed to a hospital in Enugu, where he died at about 12:30am on Wednesday. According to the source, Edochie’s family had remained at the hospital since his death, apparently attending to necessary arrangements and coming to terms with the loss. The family’s absence from the residence accounted for the quiet atmosphere observed during the reporter’s visit. item.title: Why I turned down Burna Boy’s 85/15 demand – Aristokrat boss, Peedi Picasso
item.description: By Benjamin Njoku Peedi Picasso, CEO of Aristokrat Records, has opened up on why he refused to renew Burna Boy’s record deal, saying the singer demanded an 85-15 per cent revenue split in his favour. Picasso, whose real name is Piriye Isokrari said their previous deal gave Burna Boy 60 per cent, while the label took 40 per cent. He also revealed that the singer’s mother insisted he should only sign two-year contracts, a condition that influenced the label’s decision. According to Picasso, the proposed increase did not make financial sense at the time because the label was not making significant money from record sales. Picasso said live performances and endorsement deals were the major sources of revenue. He argued that accepting an 80-20 or 85-15 split would have left the label with a smaller share of the income despite the money it was investing in the singer. Picasso said the arrangement was difficult to justify for another two-year contract, particularly because the label was not entering a long-term deal. However, he admitted that his position has changed, saying he would now accept the terms he previously rejected. “Today I will take the 85/15 per cent now, but back then, it didn’t make any sense,” he said. He also explained that Burna Boy received the larger share of performance earnings under their former agreement because he was the artiste taking the stage. item.title: Slow Turnout At Kaduna Polling Unit As INEC Holds Mock Accreditation
item.description: There is a slow turnout at polling units 031 and 032 in Ungwan Boro, Sabon Tasha ward, in Chikun Local Government Area of Kaduna State, as there is little to suggest that the mock accreditation exercise set to hold today by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is taking place. As at the time of filing this report, at exactly 9:29 am , officials of the Independent National Electoral Commission were yet to be on ground to commence the exercise scheduled to commence by 8:3am. The only security presence observed is that of three personnel of the Nigeria Security CIVIL Defence Corps (NSCDC) There is also no presence of voters at the two polling units, raising questions about the level of preparedness and awareness ahead of the exercise. The situation contrasts with INEC’s earlier assurance of readiness for the mock election, which is designed to assess its operational capacity and the effectiveness of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System and result transmission technology ahead of the 2027 general elections. As at Friday night, when voting materials were distributed at the INEC office in Kaduna, the Administrative Secretary, Abba Yahaya, also assured the public of the Commission’s readiness for the mock election, expressing confidence in its preparedness to conduct the exercise. The exercise is expected to simulate the 2027 Presidential election, with polling units opening by 8:30 a.m. and accreditation running from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. The situation is, however, slightly different at polling unit 002, located within Narayi Primary School, also in Chikun Local Government Area. As of 10 a.m., some voters were seen hanging around the polling area, awaiting the commencement of the exercise. However, as at the time of this report, INEC officials were yet to arrive, leaving the voters waiting without any indication of when the mock election would begin. item.title: Lawal pledges more projects as APC Campaign visits Shinkafi
item.description: Governor seeks support for Tinubu, APC candidates ahead of 2027 polls Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal, has pledged to execute more development projects in Shinkafi Local Government Area as he canvassed support for the All Progressives Congress (APC) ahead of the 2027 general elections. Lawal made the pledge on Friday during the APC Zamfara North campaign flag-off rally held at the Eid ground in Shinkafi. The rally attracted party chieftains, including the Director-General of the Tinubu/Shettima Presidential Campaign Council and former governor, Abdul’aziz Yari; another former governor, Mahmuda Aliyu Shinkafi; the state APC Chairman, Kabiru Moyi; and other party leaders. Tens of thousands of supporters reportedly welcomed the campaign entourage at the town’s entrance, chanting slogans in support of the party. Addressing the gathering, Lawal thanked the people of Shinkafi for their solidarity and warm reception, saying their support was encouraging. He said his administration had recorded achievements in education, healthcare, infrastructure and economic development. The governor disclosed that his administration had rehabilitated six primary healthcare centres, including facilities in Badarawa, Birnin Yero, Galadi, Jangeru and Kurya. He described the ongoing referral hospital project in Shinkafi as a legacy initiative that would transform healthcare delivery in Zamfara State and the North-West. According to him, the project is central to his administration’s commitment to improving access to quality healthcare. Lawal also said his administration had completed 22 of the 31 projects undertaken over the past three and a half years, while the remaining nine were at more than 80 per cent completion. He urged residents to support President Bola Tinubu, his administration and other APC candidates in the 2027 general elections. “I am here once again to seek your votes. Vote for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, vote for me, and vote for the APC from top to bottom in the upcoming 2027 general election,” he said. The governor’s spokesman, Sulaiman Bala Idris, disclosed this in a statement issued on November 27, 2026. item.title: Chelsea in a ‘difficult moment’ admits Alonso
item.description: Xabi Alonso admitted Chelsea are in a “difficult moment” as the beleaguered boss urged his struggling side to stick together after their dismal 3-2 defeat at Nottingham Forest on Friday. Alonso’s side crashed to a third successive Premier League loss to leave them languishing in eighth place. The Blues have lost four of their last five league matches, piling pressure on Alonso just months into his reign at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea fell behind to Igor Jesus’s early opener before Morgan Gibbs-White doubled Forest’s lead with a second half penalty. Emmanuel Emegha reduced the deficit but Gibbs-White struck again to make Emega’s late second nothing more than a footnote on another dispiriting evening for Alonso. “It’s a difficult moment for everyone. It’s disappointing again to lose again but we need to keep trying to find solutions, we can’t stop,” Alonso said. “We are low in confidence, the team is struggling to hold a result. After getting to 2-1 we have conceded and go to 3-1. “Everything is not going our way, we are responsible for that and we are responsible to find solutions.” Chelsea have already conceded 23 goals in 12 league matches and their porous defence was not helped by Alonso’s curious decision to use Ecuador midfielder Moises Caicedo in a back-three. Alonso also selected Wesley Fofana after the centre-back was forced to apologise for joking in a YouTube interview about missing a penalty during Chelsea’s League Cup defeat against Liverpool this season. The hapless Fofana was booed by angry Chelsea fans at the City Ground and conceded a penalty with his careless foul on former Blues striker Liam Delap. “We need to support everyone. Everyone that is in the team we need to support,” Alonso said of Fofana. “We know we have to go through difficult moments. We don’t take apart anyone and we want to help.” Asked to assess Chelsea’s dismal run, Alonso suggested the only cure was hard work on the training ground. “We can do better for sure. At this level you need to hold results and that is why we are losing in the last games,” he said after Chelsea’s sixth league defeat his term. “That is the only way I understand football. When things are not going well, try to work and find solutions. It can happen that we turn it around and it goes our way.” Chelsea’s sixth league defeat under Alonso will spark pointed questions about the former Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen boss. Although Alonso led Leverkusen to an historic Bundesliga title in 2024, he lasted just seven months before being sacked by Real. The former Liverpool midfielder desperately needs a win against bottom of the table Crystal Palace on Wednesday to avoid the sack talk growing even louder. “Everyone needs to stick together and go through this moment. item.title: Ten live bets, zero accumulators: the story of a bettor from Burkina Faso
item.description: No bets on impulse. No chasing miracles. An AfroPari player from Burkina Faso has made a net profit of over 14 millions $ from ten bets, all placed live. Her idea? While everyone else waits for goals, she bets there won’t be many. One match, one slip Her biggest win: over 6,800 $ on a match in Switzerland Plenty of bettors stuff their slips with five, six, even ten events, dreaming of a huge payout, but not her: one event, sensible odds. Betting on silence She watches the game, feels the tempo, and only then makes her move. She’s after tight, cagey matches where nobody wants to take risks. Most of her bets are on goals staying under a certain line, sometimes in the first half only. Best example? Hoffenheim vs Schalke 04. She backed this one twice: first the first half, then the full match. Two bets, two hits. Not just Europe, not just football Big names aren’t her thing. Europe’s top leagues, yes, but also Colombia, Hong Kong and even ice hockey. It doesn’t matter who’s playing. What matters is how the game is going. An approach, not a recipe You could look at her ten slips and see a method worth copying. It isn’t one. It’s simply how she lives the game: patience, attention, one bet at a time. And nothing was settled in advance: a last-minute goal, a penalty, a defensive slip – and everything could have turned. Above all, her story shows you don’t have to chase big odds. It doesn’t show there’s a sure way to win. Betting is still a game, and chance is never far away. When luck has the final word For those who’d rather trust fate, AfroPari runs JackPot on Sport every month. Players who bet on sports during the month, pre-match or live, and reach a total of 7,287,404 NGN. FCFA are entered into the draw. At the end of the month, 30 winners are picked at random. item.title: Amotekun arrests suspect over alleged 200 house break-ins in Ondo
item.description: …Over 200 master keys recovered from suspect By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Ondo State Security Network Agency, Amotekun Corps, has arrested a suspected serial housebreaker, identified as Michael Morayo, for allegedly breaking into more than 200 houses across different parts of the state. Morayo was among 13 suspected criminals paraded by the security outfit in Akure, the state capital. He was reportedly arrested in the Ijomu area of Akure. According to the Amotekun Corps, the suspect allegedly operated alone for about six years, breaking into houses and stealing household items, which he subsequently sold through an online marketplace he reportedly established. The security outfit said the suspect maintained an affluent lifestyle, dressed elegantly and spoke politely, making it difficult for people to suspect his alleged criminal activities. It added that he operated a warehouse where he kept stolen items and was meticulous in carrying out his operations. Parading the suspects, the State Commander of Amotekun, Chief Adetunji Adeleye, said Morayo allegedly confessed to breaking into more than 200 houses. Adeleye disclosed that over 200 master keys were recovered from him, explaining that the suspect often gained access to houses without forcing doors or breaking locks. “He does not always break doors to gain access to houses. We recovered well over 200 master keys from him. He also confessed that he usually finds ways of visiting people under different pretences. “In the process, he checks their doors and, while engaging them in conversation, removes one of their spare keys,” Adeleye said. He advised residents against keeping multiple keys in their door locks, warning that the practice could expose their homes to burglars. According to him, the suspect sometimes allegedly removed keys from doors and kept them in his pocket to gain access to the houses later. Adeleye further alleged that Morayo had other methods of gaining entry into homes, including making occupants fall asleep before stealing household equipment. The Amotekun commander said the suspect’s lifestyle and manner of presentation often shielded him from suspicion. He assured that all 13 suspects arrested and paraded by the corps would face prosecution after investigations. “After detailed investigations, they will be charged before courts of competent jurisdiction, depending on the offences they are suspected to have committed,” he said. item.title: Plateau will overcome insecurity, says Jonathan
item.description: …Hails Mutfwang’s unity initiative By Golok Nanmwa JOS — Former President Goodluck Ebele Jonathan has expressed optimism that Plateau State will overcome its lingering security challenges, describing the annual Plateau Unity Christmas Carols and Praise Festival as an important platform for reconciliation, peaceful coexistence and lasting peace. Jonathan, who commended Governor Caleb Manasseh Mutfwang for promoting unity through the annual religious gathering, spoke on Friday night at the third edition of the festival held at the Ten Commandments Prayer Altar, Jos. The festival, which began on November 27, 2026, brought together Christian leaders, traditional rulers, choristers, government officials and worshippers from within and outside the state to celebrate Christmas and promote unity among residents. The former president acknowledged the security challenges Plateau had experienced over the years but expressed confidence that the unity being promoted through the festival would help address divisions and strengthen relationships among communities. He commended the state government for sustaining the initiative, describing it as an important platform for bringing people together through worship and shared values. Jonathan also expressed confidence in Mutfwang’s commitment to promoting unity, while praying for divine intervention and the restoration of lasting peace in the state. He equally applauded former Governor Jonah David Jang for his contributions to leadership in Plateau State. Earlier, Mutfwang described the festival as a divine initiative established three years ago to unite the people under the banner of God, stressing that unity was essential to overcoming the challenges confronting the state. Declaring the event open, the governor expressed confidence in God’s protection, saying that despite the forces working against Plateau, the people would not be overwhelmed. He said: “If it were left to the forces that are arrayed against Plateau, we will not be gathered here tonight. But God has told us in His word that we will pass through the fires, we will not be consumed. We will pass through the waters, we will not be overwhelmed.” Mutfwang explained that the festival was conceived not merely as a musical celebration but as an opportunity for spiritual renewal, reconciliation and the removal of barriers to unity among residents. Citing Psalm 133:1, which states that “how good and pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity,” he expressed hope that the gathering would help break down walls of division, bitterness, hatred and mutual suspicion. He urged residents to renew their commitment to love, togetherness and the collective progress of the state. item.title: A Weekend For Proof
item.description: INEC tests its systems on Saturday. Opposition leaders face their own test on Monday. Campaign violence makes both exercises more consequential. By Tuesday, Nigerians should have fresh evidence about two institutions seeking their confidence. INEC will have conducted its nationwide mock accreditation and result-upload exercise. Opposition parties will have had their scheduled opportunity to formalise cooperation in Abuja. The first must demonstrate operational readiness. The second must demonstrate an ability to act together. Both approach those tests amid a worsening concern: whether citizens can participate in the campaign safely. Wednesday’s attack on Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) supporters in Benin City, Edo State, confirmed by the police, followed Monday’s deadly violence in Delta. Edo police reported one person injured and ordered an investigation. The attackers’ political affiliations and any sponsors have not been established. That development changes the context of the coming days. Electoral preparation now requires visible progress on protection, accountability and public confidence alongside equipment and political agreements. Saturday: Let The Test Produce Evidence INEC’s mock exercise is scheduled for November 28, from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. Nigerian time, in 17,676 selected polling units. It will test accreditation, election devices, and the uploading and viewing of simulated results. Registered voters in the selected units are expected to participate. The most useful outcome would be a public account of performance. How many locations opened on time? How many participants were successfully accredited? Where did devices fail? How long did uploads take? How were exceptions resolved? A rehearsal can reveal problems that announcements cannot. Finding a fault early allows INEC to correct it. Explaining that correction gives citizens a reason to have greater confidence. The exercise also has practical support from state governments. Lagos has cancelled Saturday’s sanitation exercise, while Anambra has postponed its own, to avoid obstructing participation. Those decisions remove an immediate obstacle. The remaining test concerns delivery at the selected polling units. Monday: What Will Opposition Unity Require? Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi, Seyi Makinde and other opposition leaders are expected at the November 30 summit. Their attendance and any signed commitments remain forthcoming. The APC says it is untroubled by the proposed gathering. The parties’ task is to define cooperation precisely. Joint election monitoring could be valuable. So could common procedures for documenting intimidation, sharing verified information and coordinating legal responses. Presidential cooperation presents more difficult choices. Supporters need to know whether their parties intend to campaign separately, endorse an existing candidate or pursue another lawful arrangement. A declaration of unity leaves those questions open unless it specifies obligations.

item.title: CHINA DIARIES: Where Students Build the Future
item.description: I must confess, I was not quite prepared for what I saw during my visit to the Qinling Workshop at Xi’an Aeronautical Vocational and Technical College in China. For someone fascinated by technology and innovation, walking into the institution’s aircraft hangar was an experience in itself. There were aircraft and helicopters, aviation equipment and specialised training facilities. For a moment, it felt less like visiting a school and more like stepping into an aviation engineering centre. But the biggest surprise was yet to come. Beyond the aircraft and helicopters, I encountered something that left an even stronger impression: drones designed, developed and assembled by students. China Diaries: The Railway Connecting Continents China Diaries: The future of farming These were not simply classroom models or academic projects put together to earn grades. The students were experimenting with different drone technologies, exploring their applications and developing solutions to practical problems. There were different designs and innovations, reflecting the creativity, technical confidence and curiosity of young people who were not waiting until graduation to start making a contribution to society. It was exciting to see. One could immediately imagine the possibilities: drones that could help farmers monitor crops and spray farmlands, support environmental monitoring, conduct aerial surveys, inspect infrastructure and assist emergency response operations. What struck me most was the philosophy behind what I was seeing. Technology was not being taught as an abstract subject. Students were being encouraged to understand problems and develop technological solutions. An institution built around practical skills The Qinling Workshop visit offered an opportunity to appreciate the work of Xi’an Aeronautical Vocational and Technical College, an institution with a strong focus on aviation, engineering and technical education. Its programmes cover a wide range of disciplines, including aviation manufacturing, aircraft maintenance, aircraft engine technology, drone application technology, general aviation, mechanical engineering, artificial intelligence, computer technology, robotics, automation, electronic information, aviation logistics and automotive technology. Students also study specialised areas such as CNC machining, intelligent manufacturing, aircraft electronic systems, materials engineering, welding technology, surveying and remote sensing, software development, big data, airport operations and civil aviation services. The breadth of these programmes is significant. It shows an understanding that an aviation and manufacturing economy requires much more than pilots and aircraft engineers. It needs technicians, software developers, mechanics, materials specialists, electronics experts, maintenance professionals and people who can design, manufacture and repair equipment.
